## Summary

**Root cause:** `solution.py` did `csv.DictReader(text.splitlines())`. `str.splitlines()` splits on *every* line ending — including LF/CRLF characters embedded inside quoted fields — before the CSV parser could see them. This destroyed multiline field content and also mixed up record boundaries.

**Fix:** Feed the text to the parser as an in-memory stream with universal-newline translation disabled, exactly as the csv module recommends for file input:

```python
return list(csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text, newline="")))
```

With `newline=""`, CRLF/LF are kept intact so `csv` can correctly distinguish record separators from embedded newlines inside quoted fields. An early `if not text: return []` short-circuit keeps the empty-input behavior explicit (header-only input already naturally yields `[]`).

The public API (`read_records(text) -> list[dict]`) is unchanged.

**Tests run:** `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` → **10 passed, 0 failed**. Existing public tests were left untouched; I added a `RegressionTests` class covering CRLF record separators, embedded LF and CRLF preservation, commas and doubled/escaped quotes, blank field values, header-only input, and multiple records with multiline fields.
